title: Dashboard accessibility and oncall annotation guidelines
summary: Working notes and lightweight guidelines for making inference dashboards easier to read, faster to act on during incidents, and accessible to non-engineering stakeholders. Focus: annotation patterns, trace linkage, metric label visibility, and keyboard-friendly panel navigation for oncall users.
purpose: Document pragmatic rules and small templates we can apply across product and infra dashboards so oncall can locate root causes faster and stakeholders can self-serve basic checks without escalating. Also capture low-effort accessibility improvements (contrast, font, keyboard focus) that measurably improve time-to-ack.
audience: Observability engineers, dashboard owners (product + infra), SRE/oncall, support leads, and partner PMs who review dashboards.
background: We get repeated feedback: dashboards are noisy, annotations are inconsistent, trace links are buried, and non-technical stakeholders misinterpret metrics. This doc collects heuristics and tiny templates that have worked in SRE handoffs and incident postmortems. Not a replacement for metric contracts, but a complement focused on operator UX.
key_guidelines: 1) Single-line intent: every dashboard must start with a one-line intent (what is this dashboard for?) placed in the top-left panel. 2) Three-tier visibility: critical top-row widgets (SLOs, error-rate, latency p50/p95), diagnostic mid-row (cache warmth, batch size, model load), and deep row (traces, logs links, release tags). 3) Use human-readable labels: prefer "time-to-first-token (ms)" over "ttft" and include units. 4) Contrast & size: use >4.5:1 color contrast for text on background for critical tiles; minimum label font 12 px. 5) Keyboard focus: ensure top-row widgets are reachable via tab order; annotate tab order in dashboard notes for panels that open modals. 6) Annotation hygiene: every deploy/rollout annotation must include: author, deploy-tag, canary-percentage, and rollback-link. 7) Trace linking: panels that show request aggregates must have a one-click "trace search" link pre-filled with span tags and time window. 8) One-line operator quickchecks: top-left card contains 3 quickchecks (cache-warm? models-healthy? throttle-active?) with green/yellow/red dots and a single Slack slash command suggestion for the common mitigation (e.g., /obs warm-cache MODEL).
annotation_patterns: Use a small vocabulary for annotations to keep things parsable by people and tools. Template for deploys: "[deploy] {service}@{sha[:7]} by {owner} env={env} canary={N}% notes={short-reason} tickets={JIRA-ID}". Template for incidents: "[incident] id={INC-####} svc={service} start={ISO8601} severity={P0|P1} owner={oncall}". Use these exact bracketed prefixes so we can parse annotations into the incident timeline exporter. When adding manual notes, always include the investigative anchor (e.g., "checked_kv_warmth", "trace-anchored:span.service=kvcache").
trace_integration_recs: 1) Default one-click trace link should pre-populate: service, operation, time window +-2min around spike, and top label/value filters (e.g., tenant, model_name). 2) For multi-model fanout panels, include a "trace-sample" button that opens a representative trace (heuristics: highest latency, highest token count, or first error). 3) Sampling budgets: for user-facing canaries sample 1:1 for 10min after rollout and drop to 1:100 thereafter; for high-volume embedding endpoints use 1:1000 baseline with adaptive bumping on anomalies. 4) Trace payload redaction: default trace link must not include PII; use session_id hashed and include a note about redaction level for each panel.
metric_definition_examples: Provide compact contract examples to reduce misinterpretation. Example A (SLO): name=ttft_successful_requests.p50; definition=median time_to_first_token for requests with 2+ tokens; units=ms; owner=serving-runtime; heatmap_panel=top-left. Example B (Cache Warmth): name=kv_cache_warmth; definition=percentage of requests that hit in-memory prefix cache; units=%; sampling=1:1000 for long-tail calculation, full-scan daily. Example C (Token cost): name=token_cost_per_request; definition=estimated $/request computed from tokens_out*price_per_token + model_inference_gpu_cost amortized; owner=optimize; note=approximate—used for alerting only when >X% deviation from baseline.
dashboard_annotation_template:
Top-left card content (markdown-ish): 
Title: Intent: 'Oncall quick-check for inference path'
One-line intent: 'Fast view for token-latency regressions and cache-health for hosted-api'
Quickchecks: 
- cache_warmth: GREEN if >95% else YELLOW/RED
- p95_ttft: GREEN if <200ms else YELLOW/RED
- model_fanout_errors: GREEN if 0 else YELLOW/RED
Runbook link: <confluence link>
Trace search: <one-click url template>
Last deploy: [deploy] serving@c3d4a1b by Priya 2026-01-08 canary=10% tickets=ENG-2891
Operator notes: 'If cache_warmth RED -> trigger /obs warm-cache MODEL; if p95 high but cpu low -> check kv-eviction and model-quantization fallback.'
rollout_checklist: Pre-rollout (owner): update dashboard top-left intent line; add deploy annotation using standard template; set canary probes as synthetic; ensure trace link is present. During rollout: monitor quickchecks card and deviation panel; maintain 1:1 trace sampling for canary window. Post-rollout: annotate canary completion and schedule metric drift check at +24h. If regression flagged, run trace-sample, save 3 representative traces to incident ticket, and add a short diagnostic note to the dashboard annotation (e.g., 'found span.service=kvcache eviction spike at T+12m').
accessibility_notes: - Color-blindness: avoid red/green-only indicators; prefer shape + color (dot + chevron). - High-contrast mode: provide an alternate color palette toggle for dashboards used in war room screens. - Screen reader affordances: ensure important metric labels include expanded descriptions in the dashboard notes (e.g., 'ttft: ms to first token, excludes warm-start latency'). - Keyboard navigation: dashboards that open modals must document focus-trap behavior in the notes and ensure ESC closes modals. - Mobile: condense top-left quickchecks into a single collapsible card for oncall mobile viewing.
todo_items: - Convert deploy/incident annotation regex into a little parser (ENGOBS-1423). - Add keyboard-tab order metadata to top 20 dashboards by end of Q1 2026. - Create a small accessibility toggle in the dashboard renderer (design + FE ticket). - Run a 1-week oncall shadow experiment to validate quickchecks reduce TL;DR slack pings. - Add a 'trace-sample' button to embed representative spans in dashboards (PR #78 in obs-dashboards repo).
open_questions: - What is the privacy boundary for trace links in private-deploy customers? (need legal check). - Should we require annotation templates at commit time (CI lint) or keep as post-deploy operator hygiene? - Do product owners want the quickchecks standardized across product dashboards or only infra?
